bug_semantics: In the administrator-only Downloads deletion action, a nonce-authenticated POST supplied file_id, file, file_name, and unlinkfile. The handler sanitized file only as text and, when unlinkfile was 1, passed the attacker-controlled value directly to unlink($file_path . $file). sanitize_text_field() does not remove ../ traversal components, so an authenticated user with the manage_downloads capability (assigned to administrators) could replace the hidden file field with traversal sequences and delete an arbitrary file reachable by the PHP process. Deleting a critical file such as wp-config.php can cause availability/integrity loss and may enable code execution through reconfiguration. The nonce and capability check prevent an unauthenticated path but do not bind the posted pathname to the selected database row.
flaw_origin: The smallest true first-writer is WordPress Subversion changeset r7446 (2007-01-21, GamerZ, log 'WP-DownloadManager First Commit'), which added trunk/downloadmanager/download-manager.php with the posted file value flowing to unlink($file_path . '/' . $file). The immediately preceding repository revision r7445 has no such path/file. The assigned Git repository's 2013 commit 8c862546f81e81283cb2afeea193a6b7ac522b50 is a later import of already-vulnerable version 1.61 and is therefore not the BIC.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC changeset object. WordPress SVN r7446 is authored by GamerZ on 2007-01-21 with log 'WP-DownloadManager First Commit'; its git-svn mirror object contains only the git-svn-id trailer and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI identity, or bot identity. No later import or fix metadata was used for the AI judgment.
evidence: Vulnerability and privilege path: in the validated clone, `git grep -n manage_downloads b8e6bd8d773baa58846cd06e3fcb72f06f7bcf56` shows download-manager.php guarding with current_user_can('manage_downloads'), wp-downloadmanager.php registering the menu with that capability, and lines 1610-1613 assigning it to the administrator role. `git blame -L 205,235 b8e6bd8d773baa58846cd06e3fcb72f06f7bcf56 -- download-manager.php` shows the vulnerable 1.69 handler: POST file is only sanitize_text_field()'d and then used by unlink($file_path.$file). The immutable release source at https://plugins.svn.wordpress.org/wp-downloadmanager/tags/1.69/download-manager.php contains the same flow. True BIC and parent: https://plugins.svn.wordpress.org/!svn/rvr/7446/wp-downloadmanager/trunk/downloadmanager/download-manager.php contains `$file = trim($_POST['file'])` followed by `unlink($file_path.'/'.$file)`; the same r7445 URL returns 404 because the path did not exist. The preserved changeset object is https://api.github.com/repos/wp-plugins/wp-downloadmanager/commits/945d225790291d995e839622d088a4f67e5bcb68: author/committer GamerZ, 2007-01-21, message 'WP-DownloadManager First Commit' plus git-svn-id r7446, parent e9aa8d23188c25a882141de5717b006d272a6d73; that parent's tree is the empty tree. In the assigned clone, `git log --follow -- download-manager.php` bottoms out at later import 8c862546f81e81283cb2afeea193a6b7ac522b50, and `git grep -n -e "unlink(\$file_path" -e "\$_POST\['file'\]" 8c862546f81e81283cb2afeea193a6b7ac522b50 -- download-manager.php` confirms the imported vulnerable lines, while the same command at parent a09241ef80dae7961961ed0bf637cfeaef23cb33 finds no file. Fix and boundary: `git show d3470a8971d9043438c8aad281cf37d14fefa208` shows the direct fix replacing POST file/file_name with a prepared SELECT by integer file_id and using the database row's file path, deleting the attacker-controlled hidden inputs, and bumping 1.69 to 1.69.1. Its direct parent is b8e6bd8d773baa58846cd06e3fcb72f06f7bcf56 and is vulnerable. `git rev-parse '1.69.1^{}'` resolves the release tag to 416b9f5459496166c0395f9e055d4c4cf872404a, whose parent is d3470a8971d9043438c8aad281cf37d14fefa208; the immutable 1.69.1 source at https://plugins.svn.wordpress.org/wp-downloadmanager/tags/1.69.1/download-manager.php fetches the row by file_id and unlinks `$file_path . $file->file`. Thus released versions 1.00 through 1.69 carry the deletion flaw and 1.69.1 is the first fixed release.
reasoning: The posted path, rather than merely the selected row ID, controlled the filesystem sink, so the root cause is failure to derive the deletion pathname from trusted server-side state. The direct fix d3470a8971d9043438c8aad281cf37d14fefa208 closes that data-flow by reloading the row by integer ID; the later 1.69.1 tag commit is a release-boundary hardening commit for a separate download_path setting and does not replace the direct fix. History predates the assigned Git import: SVN r7446 is the atomic source changeset that first adds both the untrusted POST read and unlink sink, and r7445 lacks the file, so the later 2013 import is rejected as an introducer. AI attribution is judged only on r7446's changeset metadata; it identifies a human GamerZ and contains no AI marker, and it dates to 2007. Therefore the causal result is NOT_AI.
